pr_body:
Hi,

This is my first pull request so let me know if something isn't right.

The feature proposal in issue #2143 was to expose `isNotFound` in the request object. The variable default value is false and it is automatically set to true by checking the context on the route handler. 

It works like this:

```javascript
fastify.addHook('onRequest', (req, reply, done) => {
    if (req.isNotFound) {
      reply.code(404).send(new Error('kaboom'))
    }
    done()
  })

  fastify.get('/', function (req, reply) {
    reply.send({ hello: 'world' })
  })
```

Closes: #2143

So, essentially it'd be very nice to catch that it was a 404 and just don't care about parsing the content-type or message body because it's already an invalid request based on route not matching alone.
I'd like to work on this
are there any other status codes where you would have an overlapping use case? For instance.. what about a 400?

@davidmarkclements for me, it's really about just rejecting requests from all those automated bots that try to attack & pwn literally any HTTP server on the internet, so for our use case, 404 or route not found could be a very first step: it'd allow us to kill off bot requests very early on in their lifecycle.

I'd be happy with this being a plugin too, but I don't think a plugin should use internal APIs
I think the name should be isNotFound because of parity with the serNotFoundHandler.

> what about a 400?

At that stage, the body has been already parsed (assuming the schema validation in action)

I would act in a different way, using `reply.statusCode`, since the 404 is a response domain:

In a 404 case I have
```
fastify.addHook('onRequest', (req, reply, done) => {
  console.log('onRequest', reply.statusCode) // 200
  done()
})
fastify.addHook('onResponse', (req, reply, done) => {
  console.log('onResponse', reply.statusCode) // 404
  done()
})
```

The routing should be already executed at that stage and in the `onRequest` the status code could/should (?) be already set to 404
Is there need a 404 plugin now ? if need, I will work for it 😁
No, we need a fresh PR that implements https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/2153.

review_comments:
Please avoid creating one more property in this object. This adds a few bytes of memory for each request.

You can use a getter instead.

We can’t use a getter here, as we don’t have access to the context object.
The only way would be to have it in `reply.isNotFound`, but I’m not sure is semantically correct.
I'm -1 on adding one more property to Request. We have already too many.

So are you suggesting to add it as a getter in `reply`?
If so, I'm not sure that `isNotFound` is the best name to use.
Yes. It’s ok to change name.

Right now, if we add it to reply, I don't see any improvements respect `reply.statusCode === 404`

We should only add this line in the fourOhFour.js file to set the code since the beginning

```
const onRequest = this[kHooks].onRequest.concat([(request, reply, done) => {
        reply.code(404)
        done()
      }])
```
I think it should be possible to add it as a getter to the request with a little refactoring. But I haven't had time to investigate.

@Eomm we can’t use the status code, as it is not reliable. If the user has an hook that changes the status code, the user will never know if they are inside a 404 handling or not.
We must use the internal way we are already using for identify that situation.

Here you should also add a `return` to stop the request lifecycle :)
```suggestion
      return reply.code(404).send(new Error('kaboom'))
```
